items.example: Hace buen tiempo, ¿comemos fuera?
items.example_en: The weather's nice, shall we eat outside?
items.note: Weather uses impersonal hacer, never ser or estar.

items.example: Está lloviendo desde esta mañana.
items.example_en: It's been raining since this morning.
items.note: llover is impersonal: only llueve, never yo lluevo.

items.example: Nieva en los Pirineos.
items.example_en: It's snowing in the Pyrenees.
items.note: Stem-changing: nevar becomes nieva.

items.example: Hace frío esta mañana, ponte un abrigo.
items.example_en: It's cold this morning, put on a coat.
items.note: tengo frío is about you, hace frío about the air.

items.example: ¿Qué tiempo hace ahí?
items.example_en: What's the weather like there?
items.note: One word for both weather and time. la hora is clock time.

items.example: Según la previsión, mañana va a llover.
items.example_en: According to the forecast, it's going to rain tomorrow.

items.example: En primavera todo vuelve a florecer.
items.example_en: In spring everything blooms again.
items.note: Seasons take en, without an article: en verano, en invierno.

items.example: Vamos al mar en verano.
items.example_en: We go to the sea in summer.

items.example: Vamos a la montaña este invierno.
items.example_en: We're going to the mountains this winter.
items.note: Singular in Spanish where English uses the plural.

items.example: El mar está tranquilo hoy.
items.example_en: The sea is calm today.
items.note: Usually masculine, but la mar in poetic and sailors' usage.

items.example: Paseamos por el bosque los domingos.
items.example_en: We walk in the forest on Sundays.

items.example: El cambio climático está alterando las estaciones.
items.example_en: Climate change is altering the seasons.

items.example: Es una película que he visto tres veces.
items.example_en: It's a film I've seen three times.
items.note: que is the workhorse relative pronoun for both people and things.

items.example: Siempre veo las películas en versión original.
items.example_en: I always watch films in the original language.
items.note: Marked VO or VOSE on Spanish cinema listings; Spain dubs heavily.

items.example: Pon los subtítulos en español.
items.example_en: Put the subtitles in Spanish.
items.note: Watching with target-language subtitles is excellent practice.

items.example: Empecé una novela policíaca.
items.example_en: I started a crime novel.
items.note: Also a soap opera in Latin America: la telenovela.

items.example: La serie es larga pero merece la pena.
items.example_en: The series is long but it's worth it.
items.note: In Latin America: vale la pena.

items.example: Este libro te lo recomiendo de verdad.
items.example_en: This book, I really recommend it to you.
items.note: Two pronouns stack in a fixed order: te lo.

items.example: Tengo ganas de salir esta noche.
items.example_en: I feel like going out tonight.
items.note: Followed by de plus infinitive.

items.example: Salgo con amigos el viernes.
items.example_en: I'm going out with friends on Friday.
items.note: salir con alguien alone can mean to be dating someone.

items.example: La fotografía es mi pasatiempo favorito.
items.example_en: Photography is my favourite hobby.
items.note: Also la afición, which suits sport and fandom better.

items.example: Salimos de fiesta hasta las tres.
items.example_en: We partied until three.
items.note: In Spain, that is an early night.

items.example: Un cine esta noche, ¿te apetece?
items.example_en: A film tonight, do you fancy it?
items.note: Backwards like gustar. In Latin America: ¿tienes ganas?

items.example: ¿Dónde quedamos y a qué hora?
items.example_en: Where and when shall we meet?
items.note: quedar means to arrange to meet, a very Spanish use of the verb.

items.example: En mi opinión, es una mala idea.
items.example_en: In my opinion, that's a bad idea.
items.note: Neutral and safe in any register.

items.example: Creo que el debate carece de matices.
items.example_en: I think the debate lacks nuance.
items.note: Affirmative creo que takes the indicative; no creo que takes the subjunctive.

items.example: Me parece que la situación ha cambiado.
items.example_en: It seems to me the situation has changed.
items.note: Softer than creo, useful when you want room to be wrong.

items.example: Estoy convencido de que va a funcionar.
items.example_en: I'm convinced it's going to work.
items.note: The de is obligatory; dropping it is a common native error too.

items.example: Dicho esto, el coste sigue siendo un problema.
items.example_en: That said, the cost is still a problem.
items.note: Signals the concession that follows.

items.example: Es caro; en cambio, dura muchos años.
items.example_en: It's expensive; on the other hand, it lasts for years.
items.note: sin embargo is the more formal however.

items.example: Estoy de acuerdo contigo en eso.
items.example_en: I agree with you on that.
items.note: estar de acuerdo, and contigo is a single fused word.

items.example: Sinceramente, no me convence.
items.example_en: Honestly, it doesn't convince me.
items.note: Polite disagreement without confrontation.

items.example: Es cierto que hay riesgo, pero no hacer nada también lo tiene.
items.example_en: It's true there's risk, but doing nothing has risk too.
items.note: The classic concession move in an argument.

items.example: Es necesario que seamos realistas con los plazos.
items.example_en: We need to be realistic about the deadlines.
items.note: Impersonal es necesario que forces the subjunctive: seamos.

items.target: si pudiera elegir, lo haría de otra manera
items.english: if I could choose, I'd do it differently
items.pronunciation: /si puˈðje.ɾa e.leˈxiɾ lo aˈɾi.a de ˈo.tɾa maˈne.ɾa/
items.example: Si pudiera elegir, lo haría de otra manera.
items.example_en: If I could choose, I'd do it differently.
items.note: si plus past subjunctive pairs with the conditional. Never si podría.

items.example: Sea como sea, hay que decidir hoy.
items.example_en: Be that as it may, we have to decide today.
items.note: A fixed doubled-subjunctive expression, common in speech and writing.
